question:
The figure below is constructed from \(11\) line segments, each of which has length \(2.\) The area of pentagon \(ABCDE\) can be written as \(\sqrt{m} + \sqrt{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers. What is \(m + n ?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2021_AMC_10B_Q20_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The equal segments form two rhombuses, whose diagonals will give useful lengths and heights. Name the left interior point \(F\) and the right interior point \(G\). Draw \(AC\) and \(AD\); these divide the pentagon into triangles \(ABC\), \(ACD\), and \(ADE\).

Quadrilateral \(ABCG\) has four sides of length \(2\), so it is a rhombus. Let its diagonals intersect at \(P\). Rhombus diagonals perpendicularly bisect each other. Since the drawn segment \(BG\) has length \(2\), we have \(BP=1\). Applying the Pythagorean theorem to right triangle \(ABP\) gives
\[
AP=\sqrt{2^2-1^2}=\sqrt{3},
\qquad AC=2\sqrt{3}.
\]
Also, \(BP\) is the height of triangle \(ABC\) to base \(AC\), so
\[
[ABC]=\frac12(2\sqrt{3})(1)=\sqrt{3}.
\]
Here brackets denote area.

Likewise, \(AEDF\) is a rhombus with side length \(2\) and diagonal \(EF=2\). The same reasoning gives \(AD=2\sqrt{3}\) and \([ADE]=\sqrt{3}\).

Now triangle \(ACD\) is isosceles, with equal sides \(2\sqrt{3}\) and base \(CD=2\). Its altitude bisects the base, so its height is
\[
h=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{3})^2-1^2}=\sqrt{11}.
\]
Thus \([ACD]=\frac12(2)\sqrt{11}=\sqrt{11}\). Adding the three triangular areas gives
\[
[ABCDE]=2\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{11}
=\sqrt{12}+\sqrt{11}.
\]
Therefore \(m+n=12+11=\boxed{23}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
